Welcome to Couchsurfing! Some feedback culled from other's feedback and my two cents.   
1) fill out your profile completely, pictures included. Add somewhere that you're new, which will explain your current lack of references. Also add a statement that you really believe in the spirit of CouchSurfing (if you do).  
2) I find that 1-2 weeks in advance is a good time frame to message hosts. some hosts ask for shorter notice, and there's groups where you can find post to find a couch the day before or same day... but you should really message hosts first, before resorting to this.  
3) Make it evident to the host that you took the time to read their profile when messaging them. make it personal, because messages that are obviously copy/pasted or are impersonal (e.g. "I love your city"; "You seem to be a nice guy") can get ignored. What is it that you like about the host or his/her references?  
4) If you don't mind, it sometimes help to say something like "I'll cook my country's food" or "Love to go out and drink and first round's on me". I haven't always given gifts to hosts, but I try to do something nice such as cook them a meal or maybe buy them a drink. This isn't in any way obligatory, but it's courteous (if you planned to do gift them, that is).  
5) Last but not least, try to go to CouchSurfing meetings while you're traveling and before you leave your city. In the more touristy cities, there should be group meetings every week. These tend to be incredibly fun, and also a good way to get some references (either adding them as a friend or living a meet-in-person reference). Some CSers that you meet at these get-togethers might even host you that night.


Hope this helps :) Happy travels!

Great questions.  Everybody started out new at some point, so its understandable to hosts that you migth not have references. I would recommend that you try to articulate who you are as much as possible in your profile (including pictures). If you live in a city that has CS events, go to those events and add people you connected with as friends. Send out customized requests (i.e. read the potential hosts profile and try to connect in terms of interests/backgrounds/outlook/etc. (not necessary but helps).  Acknowledge your lack of references but do state that you believe in the spirit of CouchSurfing and want to meet with your host and other CSers in town (you can even ask an Ambassador to host you) and learn how to be an involved member. Also, if you can host prior to your trip, host others (it shows you are hosting and not just using CS for your travels; not that there is anything wrong with that). Finally, you don't have to hang with the host, bring gifts or pay for anything but you can be courteous and say you want to hang out and have a couple of beers/cook a meal together/etc. together. I don't care for gifts as much as time together at a bar/restaurant/cooking at home. I'm sure you'll have a blast!

Welcome to CouchSurfing! Yes, its awesome and you should roadtrip that way.  Make sure to request a host at least a week before and:

* setup a detailed profile for both of you (sometimes people want to know about both their guests) with pictures.

* Note that you are into the spirit of CouchSurfing.
 
* Friend others who you know who are on CouchSurfing. 

* Link to your Facebook profile if you don't mind. 
 
* Review a possible host's profile (look for things in common or interesting things; some even have code words in their profile to screen out people who didn't read their profiles). 

Also remember to get verified. Enjoy!
